evidence.note: Only real planning: a flat sequential to-do ('Step 1 install, Step 2 server code, Step 3 frontend, Step 4 start.sh'). Trivial ordering with no dependency reasoning about seq authority, fan-out, node-kill, or IRC bridging, and no done-conditions per milestone.

Treats the entire multi-subsystem backend as one undifferentiated lump appended into a single server.py (channels, messages, WS, IRC, cross-node broadcast all at once) — no milestone with a verifiable exit criterion, no ordering of the risky distributed invariants.

After launch the terminal hangs; ~150 near-identical 'terminal is stuck' recovery steps with zero milestone tracking, no re-planning of build ordering, and no subsystem ever verified — any early structure is fully abandoned.

reasoning: The agent produced only a flat, feature-oriented to-do list with the trivial deps→server→frontend→start.sh ordering; it never dependency-ordered or attached done-conditions to the hard distributed pieces (dense seq authority, cross-node fan-out, node-kill survival, IRC bridge), instead dumping all subsystems into one file — squarely anchor 3. It falls below anchor 5 because the risky distributed sequencing was not reasoned at all, and the milestone structure evaporated entirely once the trajectory devolved into a long unstructured terminal-recovery loop.
